children: Salesforce, Inc. (NYSE:CRM) beat Q2 FY27 expectations with $11.35B revenue, raised FY guide, and strong cash flow while adding consumption pricing, scaling Agentforce (450+ firms, 55M monthly convos) and deeper Anthropic ties, driving an ~11% premarket jump and bullish trader sentiment.
: Salesforce (CRM) Q2 FY27: revenue $11.35B (+11% YoY), subscription $10.8B (+12%), adj EPS $5.90, cRPO $33.5B (+14% CC), operating cash flow $1.3B, FCF $1.1B, raised FY revenue guide to $46.1–46.4B.
: Salesforce (CRM) shifted to a hybrid pricing model adding consumption-based fees and launched a headless agent-focused platform enabling integration and use by non-Salesforce agents.
: Salesforce (CRM): Agentforce now used by 450+ firms, including McAfee; U.S. Army handles ~55M Agentforce conversations monthly; ~5M AI autonomous service interactions; ~2.5M cases escalated.
: Salesforce's deeper Anthropic tie highlights its data, apps and governance as the channel for customers to use frontier AI models, reducing fears the models could sideline Salesforce (CRM).
: Options imply a ~7.8% move for Salesforce (CRM) around earnings, about $16.25 expected, pricing post-report shares roughly high-$190s to low-$220s, signaling wide trader expectations.
: Salesforce (CRM) rehired AI leaders Kaylin Voss and Peter Doolan; the move came alongside stronger Q2 profit and an ~11% premarket jump in shares.
: Salesforce (CRM) posted strong results, boosting software sector stocks. Peer gains and a rise in software ETF reflected broader tech strength; social sentiment for CRM grew notably bullish.
